western.temperament: Leo is read as warm, proud, generous and built to be seen: creative self-expression, loyalty, a big heart, and a need for real recognition. The traditional shadow is pride, stubbornness and wounded dignity when ignored.
western.planet: Sun (the only sign ruled by the Sun)
western.modality: Fixed (the sustained flame, not the spark); opposite sign Aquarius

chinese.temperament: Tiger people are traditionally described as brave, competitive, confident and unpredictable, natural leaders, with a shadow of being impetuous, irritable and overindulgent.
chinese.element: Wood (fixed element); earthly branch 寅 yín
chinese.clash: Monkey (Wikipedia also lists Snake as a rival)
chinese.lucky: Colors blue, grey, orange (avoid gold, silver). Numbers 1, 3, 4 (avoid 6, 7, 8). China Highlights adds flowers: yellow lily, cineraria.

symbolism.meaning: Both the English name and the genus Harpia come from Greek harpyia, the harpies: wind spirits who carried the dead away to Hades or Tartarus. The bird was named for a soul-snatcher of the air.

The character 鹰 yīng covers eagles, hawks and falcons. An eagle stands for strength, boldness and keen sight; eagle tail feathers were a protective charm; an eagle on a rock reads as a lonely struggle, an eagle in a pine as strength into old age. Painted together, eagle (yīng) and bear (xióng) make the rebus 英雄 yīngxióng, 'hero'.
Hixkaryana men hold that spiritual power lives in the hair; they hang harpy eagle feathers from feathered hair tubes to strengthen that power and connect to the spirit world.

Harpy feathers and talons were coveted as symbols of power, and the bird was held in a mix of fear and awe. ADW notes occasional use in ceremonial rituals by Indigenous hunters. In many South American cultures cutting down the kapok tree, a favored nest tree, is considered bad luck.
National bird of Panama and shown on its coat of arms; ADW adds the state bird of Paraná, Brazil.
Wikipedia states the harpy eagle was sacred to Quetzalcoatl. Single secondary claim with no primary source checked: verify before use.
Unsourced, do not use. Found only on a lore blog with no claim-level citation (hitchhikersguidetoreligion.com).

fusion.temperament: Our reading: Leo is a fixed Fire sign ruled by the Sun, made to be seen; the Tiger is yang Wood, brave, solitary and quick to strike. Wood feeds Fire, so the Tiger half literally fuels the Leo half. The Harpy Eagle person carries a large presence they choose not to spend. They watch first, decide once, and then commit with their whole weight. The crest is the tell: when they care, it shows, even if they say nothing.
fusion.gifts: Our reading: patience that is actually attention; loyalty that compounds over years; the nerve to act alone once sure; a steadying effect on a room or a team once they decide to stay.
fusion.shadow: Our reading: pride that hides as stillness. Leo needs recognition and the Tiger refuses to ask for it, so this person can wait for years to be noticed rather than say what they want. Tiger impetuousness shows up as the rare, sudden, too-big reaction after a long silence. Territory can harden into control.
fusion.love: Our reading: slow to choose, then for keeps. They court by protecting and providing, not by talking. They need a partner who can tell quiet from cold, and who says out loud that they see them. Jealousy is about territory more than about feelings. Two eggs, one chick: they would rather give one person everything than share themselves thinly.
fusion.money: Our reading: a nest builder. Tends to hold one big asset (a home, a business, a single long position) and add to it for years instead of chasing many small bets. Risk: Tiger impulse and Leo generosity produce occasional large splurges after long restraint.
fusion.conflict: Our reading: goes silent and watches, which others misread as calm. When they finally move, it is one decisive act, and it can land harder than intended. Best practice for them: name the issue while it is small. Metal (a clear deadline, a plain boundary) helps them in the site's own Wu Xing frame.

careers.path: Founder or head of a small, tight operation
careers.why: Leo wants the center; the Tiger is traditionally suited to leading (China Highlights). They do best owning one territory outright.

careers.path: Surgeon, pilot, emergency or tactical roles
careers.why: Long scanning, then one precise act under pressure. China Highlights lists pilot among Tiger careers.

careers.path: Investigator, analyst, trader with long holding periods
careers.why: Working stillness: watching a field for a long time before committing capital or a conclusion.
Holding and defending ground; the throne-tree loyalty to one place.

careers.path: Performer, director or writer who works in long cycles
careers.why: Leo visibility plus Tiger artistry (actor, writer, artist all appear on the Tiger career list), released rarely and big.

best_matches.reason: Aries x Dog. Dog is in the Tiger trine and Aries is Fire. A loud, social partner who draws the eagle out.

best_matches.name: Caracara
best_matches.reason: Sagittarius x Dog. Trine partner plus Fire with Fire; a bold, roaming match that respects territory.

best_matches.name: Roseate Spoonbill
best_matches.reason: Libra x Pig. Pig is the Tiger's secret friend, and Libra's Air feeds Leo's Fire. The gentlest good match on the wheel for this animal.

best_matches.name: Moon Bear
best_matches.reason: Cancer x Tiger. Symbolic pairing: eagle (yīng) plus bear (xióng) is the Chinese rebus for 英雄 yīngxióng, hero. Same Tiger year. Element note: Water and Fire sun signs, so it is a bond of meaning more than ease.

hard_matches.name: Raven
hard_matches.reason: Aquarius x Monkey. Tiger and Monkey are one of the six clashes, and Aquarius is Leo's opposite sign. Magnetic, argumentative, hard to settle.

hard_matches.name: Regal Jumping Spider
hard_matches.reason: Leo x Monkey. Same sun sign, but the Tiger-Monkey clash: two Leos competing for the same crown, one of them restless and clever.

candidate_lines: You tend to know what you want long before anyone sees you move toward it.
There are times when people mistake your quiet for distance, when really you have not stopped paying attention for a second.
You often love by guarding. You will hold a place for someone for years and only rarely say so out loud.
Your name comes from the harpies, spirits that carried souls away on the wind. When you finally commit, you tend to take someone's whole heart with you.
In old Chinese paintings the eagle and the bear together spell hero. You tend to feel most like yourself when you are protecting something bigger than you.
You often build one nest and keep adding to it. Starting over somewhere new costs you more than people realize.

fact_audit.fact: Headline: 'The largest eagle in the world'
fact_audit.note: Contested. ADW calls it the largest species, but Wikipedia says only that it is 'sometimes cited as the largest eagle alongside the Philippine eagle', and BBC Wildlife says the title is often claimed for Steller's sea eagle, with harpy and Philippine eagles roughly as heavy (up to about 10 kg). The page also contradicts itself on the next line ('largest eagle in the Americas'). Fix: 'the largest eagle in the Americas' or 'among the heaviest eagles alive'.

fact_audit.fact: Intro: 'too heavy and short-winged to soar the way its relatives do'
fact_audit.note: Not stated in any source checked. Safer: broad, relatively short wings suited to moving through the canopy.

fact_audit.fact: 01 The crown: double row of dark feathers rises when alert; field mark separating it from the Crested Eagle
fact_audit.note: Double crest is confirmed (Wikipedia); ADW says the crown feathers rise 'when threatened', not simply when alert. The Crested Eagle field-mark comparison was not confirmed in sources checked.

fact_audit.fact: 02 The talons: up to 12.5 cm, among the largest of any living eagle; legs subdue prey 'many times heavier'
fact_audit.note: 12.5 cm is ADW's figure; Wikipedia gives mean 12.3 cm in females and 'the largest talons of any living eagle'. The 'many times heavier' prey phrasing is unsupported: typical prey (sloths, monkeys) is roughly the eagle's own weight range. Cut that clause.

fact_audit.fact: 03 The waiting: perches motionless up to 23 hours scanning for sloths and monkeys
fact_audit.note: ADW: 'can potentially perch for up to 23 hours in search of prey.' Wikipedia only says it perches for long periods. Keep the hedge 'reportedly'.

fact_audit.fact: 04 The throne tree: nest about 1.2 m thick and 1.5 m across, reused year after year
fact_audit.note: Dimensions match ADW and Wikipedia. Wikipedia says nests 'may be used over several years'; since pairs breed only every 2 to 3 years, 'year after year' slightly overstates it. Suggest 'season after season'.

fact_audit.fact: 05 The one chick: up to two eggs, one chick raised, fledges 6 to 7 months, about 10 months of care, breeds every 2 to 3 years
fact_audit.note: Matches ADW. Wikipedia: fledges at 6 months, parents keep feeding for another 6 to 10 months, so 'about ten months total' is the low end.

fact_audit.fact: 06 The territory: home range about 30 sq km, drives out competitors, pairs bond for life
fact_audit.note: ADW gives about 30 sq km and 'pairs that last for life'. Wikipedia gives about 43 sq km average (25 in fragmented forest) and says they are 'believed to' mate for life. Keep 'roughly' and consider 'believed to'.

fact_audit.fact: Hero glyph 鷹 shown with no pinyin
fact_audit.note: Owner rule: Chinese characters need pinyin with tone marks. Add yīng. Note 鷹 is the traditional form; simplified is 鹰.
